# Bootstrap a test statistic

<small>Source: [`R/bootstrap_methods.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/R/bootstrap_methods.R) · Help: `?bootstrapTestStatistic`</small>

Provides a consistent wrapper around bootstrap resampling for test
statistics produced by heteroscedasticity diagnostics. The routine
refits the supplied model on each bootstrap replicate and evaluates
`test_function` on it, returning the bootstrap distribution, a
percentile interval, and—for null-imposed resampling—a p-value.

## Usage

```r
bootstrapTestStatistic(
  test_function,
  model,
  data,
  B = 999,
  parallel = FALSE,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  resample = c("null", "pairs"),
  n_cores = NULL,
  progress = interactive(),
  ...,
  reestimate_weights = NULL
)

rbootstrap_test_statistic(
  test_function,
  model,
  data,
  B = 999,
  parallel = FALSE,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  resample = c("null", "pairs"),
  n_cores = NULL,
  progress = interactive(),
  ...,
  reestimate_weights = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

`test_function`
:   A function that accepts `(model, data, ...)` and
    returns an object with a numeric `statistic` element (typically an
    `htest` result).

`model`
:   A fitted model of class `lm`, with or without weights. A `glm`
    is rejected: each replicate is refitted with least squares, which would
    discard its family and link.

`data`
:   Data frame used when fitting `model`, holding the rows it was
    fitted to under their row names. Other rows are left out. See Details.

`B`
:   Integer, number of bootstrap replications. Defaults to 999. The
    p-value is `(1 + #) / (B_eff + 1)`, so a test at level `alpha` is exact
    only when `alpha * (B + 1)` is an integer: with 999 it is at the 5% and
    1% levels, and with 1000, the default before 0.15.0, at neither.

`parallel`
:   Logical, compute replicates in parallel when possible? See
    *Parallel replicates*.

`ci_level`
:   Confidence level for the percentile interval.

`resample`
:   Bootstrap strategy. `"null"` (the default) regenerates
    the response under homoscedasticity and yields a testable `p_value`;
    `"pairs"` samples rows of `data` with replacement and yields
    replicates and an interval but no p-value. See Details.

`n_cores`
:   Optional integer specifying the number of worker processes to
    use when `parallel = TRUE`. Defaults to `parallel::detectCores() - 1`.
    The result does not depend on it.

`progress`
:   Logical flag controlling whether a textual progress bar is
    displayed during bootstrap replication.

`...`
:   Additional arguments forwarded to `test_function`.

`reestimate_weights`
:   Whether each replicate estimates the weights of a
    [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md) fit again from the variance function `fitWLS()` recorded on it.
    `NULL`, the default, does so for a `fitWLS()` fit and holds the weights
    fixed for any other model. `FALSE` holds them fixed, as every call did
    before 0.15.0. `TRUE` is an error for a model that `fitWLS()` did not
    return, or on which it fell back to equal weights. Each replicate
    regenerates the response and holds the design fixed, so a variance
    regressor that uses a variable of the response which the right-hand side
    of the model does not use, such as `y` or `x` for `I(y / x) ~ z`, or that
    is the response term itself, as `~ .` gives, cannot be estimated again:
    `NULL` then holds the weights fixed, with a warning, and `TRUE` is an
    error. Giving the response as a column of the data, as in `r ~ z`, says
    which variables stay. It comes after `...`, so it has to be named in
    full. See Details.

## Value

A list with components:

`original`
:   Result returned by `test_function` on the
    original data.

`original_statistic`
:   Numeric value of the test statistic from
    the original sample.

`replicates`
:   Numeric vector of bootstrap statistics.

`ci`
:   Percentile interval of the bootstrap distribution of the
    statistic, at `ci_level`. This summarises where the resampled statistic
    falls; it is not a confidence interval for a parameter and carries no
    coverage guarantee.

`p_value`
:   Empirical p-value from the null-imposed replicates,
    computed as \((1 + \#\{T^*_b \ge T\}) / (B_{\mathrm{eff}} + 1)\);
    `NA` when `resample = "pairs"`.

`B`
:   Requested number of replications.

`effective_samples`
:   Number of non-missing bootstrap
    replications.

`call`
:   Matched call for reproducibility.

## Details

The `resample` argument decides what the replicates mean.

With `resample = "null"` (the default) the response is regenerated as
\(\hat y_i + e^*_i\), where the \(e^*_i\) are drawn with replacement from
the model's residuals after dividing by \(\sqrt{1 - h_i}\) and centring.
Those data satisfy homoscedasticity by construction, so the replicates
estimate the null distribution and `p_value` is a test. The leverage
correction matters: OLS residuals have variance \(\sigma^2 (1 - h_i)\), and
resampling them unscaled under-disperses the regenerated errors, which
inflates the rejection rate.

With `resample = "pairs"` rows are sampled with replacement. The
replicates then follow the statistic's distribution under whatever variance
structure the data actually have, which is useful for describing its
variability but is not a null distribution: the replicates are centred on the
observed statistic, so comparing the two returns roughly 0.5 whatever the
data. Measured rejection under \(\sigma_i = x_i^2\) was 0%.
`p_value` is therefore `NA` for pairs resampling.

Neither strategy accepts a `glm`: each replicate is refitted with least
squares, so the family and link would be discarded and the replicates would
describe a different model from the one supplied.

A weighted `lm` is resampled on the scale where its null hypothesis is
constant variance, the regression of \(\sqrt{w_i}\, y_i\)
on \(\sqrt{w_i}\, x_i\). Null-imposed resampling draws the
\(e^*_i\) from the Pearson residuals
\(\sqrt{w_i}\, e_i\), divided by
\(\sqrt{1 - h_i}\) with the leverages of that regression and
centred, and divides each draw by \(\sqrt{w_i}\) before adding
it to \(\hat y_i\).
Pairs resampling draws each row with its weight. Either way each replicate
is refitted with the weights, so `test_function` sees a weighted fit, as it
did on the original data.

Weights given to the fit are known, and they are held fixed. On a fit
returned by [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md) they were estimated from the same data, and since
0.15.0 each replicate estimates them again by default
(`reestimate_weights`), so that `test_function` sees what `fitWLS()` would
have returned for the replicate. The replicate is fitted as the model
`fitWLS()` was given, without weights or with the weights that model had.
The variance function `fitWLS()` recorded is fitted again to its residuals,
with the same form and on the regressors `fitWLS()` evaluated, whose rows
follow the rows drawn under pairs resampling, and the replicate is refitted
with the weights it gives. A replicate whose variance function cannot be
fitted, where `fitWLS()` would fall back to equal weights, fails as a
replicate whose refit fails does, and the p-value and the interval are
computed from the replicates that remain; a warning gives the number that
failed. In
`inst/validation/weighted-fits-size.R`, with the variance function
correctly specified, normal errors, 150 observations, `B = 499` and
[`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md) as `test_function`, the rejection rate at the 5%
level was 0.083 with the weights held fixed, as every call did before
0.15.0 and `reestimate_weights = FALSE` still does, 0.045 with them
estimated again, and 0.045 with the true weights. See the section on
weighted fits in [`performWildBootstrapTest()`](performWildBootstrapTest.md).

Weighted or not, each replicate is refitted with an offset the model was
given as an argument, `lm(..., offset = o)`; an offset written in the
formula, `offset(o)`, is evaluated again from the data of the replicate.
The rows of `data` are matched to those of the fit by row name, so that
each row is regenerated, or drawn, with its own fitted value, weight and
offset. Rows the model was not fitted to, such as those it dropped for
missing values, are left out, for the observed statistic as for the
replicates; the rows that stay keep the order of `data`. `data` that lacks
a row the model was fitted to is refused. Data without row names of its
own, such as a tibble or a data.table, that has as many rows as the fit is
taken in the order of the fit. The model is then refitted to the rows of
`data`, and `data` is refused when that refit does not give the residuals
of the fit to a relative `1e-8`: rows in another order taken by position,
values that differ from those the model was fitted to, or a variable the
formula finds outside `data`, which keeps the order of the fit. Pairs
resampling of a model with such a variable, for example `offset(o)` with
`o` in the environment of the formula, is refused too; give such an offset
as an argument instead.

Null-imposed resampling additionally requires the response to be a plain
variable. For `log(y) ~ x` the fitted values are on the log scale while
the data column holds `y`, so regenerating one from the other and
refitting would take the logarithm twice. That case raises an error;
`resample = "pairs"` resamples rows and is unaffected by it.

## Parallel replicates

With `parallel = TRUE` replicate `i` draws its random numbers from stream
`i` of a L'Ecuyer-CMRG generator ([`parallel::nextRNGStream()`](https://rdrr.io/r/parallel/RngStream.html)), seeded by
one number drawn from the session's generator. A call made after
`set.seed()` therefore returns the same result each time, whatever
`n_cores` and whether the workers are forked ([`parallel::mclapply()`](https://rdrr.io/r/parallel/mclapply.html)) or
run on a socket cluster ([`parallel::makeCluster()`](https://rdrr.io/r/parallel/makeCluster.html), where the platform
cannot fork). It does not return the result of the same call with
`parallel = FALSE`, which draws every replicate from the session's
generator, as it did before 0.15.0: the two are bootstraps of the same data
with different draws, and each is valid. Before 0.15.0 a seeded call with
`parallel = TRUE` gave a different result each time.

## Deprecated name

`rbootstrap_test_statistic()` is deprecated since 0.14.0: use
`bootstrapTestStatistic()`, the same function under the package's naming
scheme. The old name still works, returns what it returned and warns.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm`, unweighted or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since
0.16.0, a rank-deficient `lm`; a replicate whose refit aliases a coefficient the fit estimated,
as a pairs resample of an interaction can, fails. It refuses every `glm`, as each replicate is
refitted by least squares, a fit with a zero weight, and `data` that do not reproduce the fit.
Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in [`test_results`](test_results.md), under
*Supported models*.

## Examples

```r
data(mtcars)
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars)
if (interactive()) {
  set.seed(123)
  boot <- bootstrapTestStatistic(performWhiteTest, model, mtcars, B = 100)
  boot$ci
}
```
